claims.text: Interlock reads revision-bound environment evidence before shared-state mutation and selects a deterministic coordination decision.
Without Interlock the two intents produce 140 > 130, an invalid joint state against the bound sum(services[].reserved) <= 130.
With Interlock enabled and the original evidence, the decision is WITHHOLD_SERIALIZE and the joint outcome is 120 <= 130.
The controlled local experiment reports 24/24 checks.
Changing the environment evidence changes the decision to ALLOW_PARALLEL and returns the joint outcome to 140 > 130.
Each arm is a recorded result; the perturbation is a frozen arm, not a live re-run.
The cockpit screenshots are real captures of the merged HAC-341 verification surface at the stated deep-link addresses.
HAC-330 and HAC-340 are two separate runs with separate evidence. Neither is evidence for the other.
One recorded traversal ran gemini-3.5-flash through Google ADK 1.35.1 with Vertex AI access, from a Cloud Run-hosted agent in us-central1, through the Interlock MCP proxy.
Interlock returned ALLOW with an authorization receipt; the protected mutation is EXECUTED.
A separately authenticated principal read the result back and OBSERVED alpha=45, correlated in Cloud Logging by run id.
Three fail-closed refusals were recorded: a forged identity header returned 403, an invalid bearer token returned 401, and a direct target bypass without a receipt returned 403.
Three recorded refusals are three controls, not comprehensive attack coverage.
Cloud Run IAM establishes transport provenance. It does not establish Google-managed proposer, reviewer or authorizer roles inside Interlock.
interlock-hac340-proxy-00002-wzf is the only deployment revision the frozen record names. Agent and target revision names are not evidenced and are not shown.

claims.text: On a frozen sixteen-scenario corpus, four coordination strategies compare as: Uncoordinated 2/2 hazards unsafe and 2/2 independent opportunities parallel; Global lock 0/2 and 0/2; Per-target lock 2/2 and 2/2; Interlock 0/2 and 2/2.

The per-target lock baseline is credible rather than a straw man: it serialized same-target contention 2/2, parallelised cross-target pairs 4/4, and missed cross-target hazards 2/2. A composition hazard spanning two lock keys is not visible to any per-key discipline.
Interlock's safety in this corpus is evidence-derived: with coupling evidence present it produced 0/2 invalid outcomes, and with that evidence removed the same core produced 2/2 invalid outcomes.

Interlock is not 0% unsafe, is not safer than locking, and the sixteen-scenario corpus is not collapsed into one denominator. No interval or statistical significance is claimed, and no exactly-once, restart-safety or production-readiness result was tested.
Interlock is new work created during the contest, built on the pre-existing open-source workspace.json specification and toolchain consumed at pinned revisions and never copied.
